title: Grade 9 Chemistry National Exam & Practice 2018 (7 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 7 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: Which branch of chemistry deals about the effect and fate of chemical productions in the surrounding?
questions.explanation: Environmental chemistry studies the behavior and effects of chemicals in air, water, soil, and living systems.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following diagram:

Which element in the periodic table is represented by the above electronic configuration diagram?
questions.explanation:
2 + 7 = 9 electrons.
 Atomic number 9 is fluorine (F).

questions.questionText: How many protons and electrons are found in an atom of argon (Ar) with atomic number 18 and mass number 40, respectively?
questions.explanation: Atomic number 18 means 18 protons. A neutral atom has equal protons and electrons, so it has 18 electrons.

questions.questionText: According to Mendeleev's periodic law, which of the following determines the properties of elements?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev's periodic law states that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic weights.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is CORRECT about periods in the modern periodic table?
options: They are vertical columns of elements in the periodic table.
There are seven periods in the periodic table of elements.
The first three periods in the periodic table are known as long periods.
They start with alkali metals and end with alkaline earth metals.
questions.explanation: Periods are horizontal rows, and the modern periodic table has 7 periods.

questions.questionText: Why does atomic radius increase when we go down the group in the periodic table? This is because
questions.explanation: Moving down a group adds electron shells, increasing the distance of valence electrons from the nucleus.

questions.questionText: A certain element has atomic number of 33 and mass number of 75. What is the position of this element in the modern Periodic Table?
questions.explanation: Z = 33 is arsenic, with configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰4s²4p³. Therefore, it belongs to the p-block.

questions.questionText:
Given the following periodic table,

To which one of the following do the elements Li to Ne belong? They are in the same
questions.explanation: Li through Ne occupy the same horizontal row, so they are all in Period 2.

questions.questionText: In which one of the following conditions, does an ion formed from an atom?
options: When the number of electrons in an atom are less than number of protons.
When the number of electrons in an atom are equal with number of protons.
When the number of neutrons in an atom are equal with number of protons.
When the number of neutrons in an atom are greater than number of protons.
questions.explanation:
An ion forms when electrons are gained or lost.

 If electrons < protons, the atom becomes a positive ion (cation).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is TRUE about masses of subatomic particles?
options: The mass of an atom is equally distributed throughout its space.
The three subatomic particles are equal in their absolute masses.
The relative mass of a neutron is greater than that of an electron.
The relative mass of a neutron is equal with that of an electron.
questions.explanation:
A neutron has relative mass ≈ 1, while an electron has relative mass ≈ 1/1836.
 Therefore, a neutron is much heavier.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following diagram:


Which of the following bond formations is represented by the above diagram?
questions.explanation: An electron is transferred from one atom to another, forming oppositely charged ions. Their electrostatic attraction forms an ionic bond.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a covalent molecule?
questions.explanation: HBr consists of two non-metals sharing electrons, forming a polar covalent molecule.

questions.questionText: The bond in Sodium chloride (NaCl) is considered to have a great percentage of:
questions.explanation: The large electronegativity difference between Na and Cl makes the bond predominantly Ionic.

questions.questionText: If you observe a yellow flame when a certain chemical substance burns, this observation is a record of a:
questions.explanation: A qualitative observation describes a property or change using non-numerical terms, such as color, smell, or state. A quantitative measurement involves numbers and units.

questions.questionText: Precision in measurement is defined as:
options: How close a measurement is to the true value.
The reproducibility or closeness of a set of measurements to each other.
The extent of random error in a measurement.
The smallest unit of the measuring instrument.
questions.explanation: Precision refers to the repeatability of a measurement. If multiple trials yield very similar results, the measurement is considered precise.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the reducing agent in the following reaction: 8NH3 (g) + 6NO2 (g) --> 7N2 (g) + 12H2O (l)
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: In the modern periodic table, what is the name of the group that contains the most electronegative elements?
questions.explanation:
The halogens (Group 17) are the most electronegative elements because they have seven valence electrons and are highly eager to gain one more electron to complete their octet.

 Fluorine, the top halogen, is the **most electronegative element** in the periodic table.

 Alkali metals are highly electropositive, chalcogens are moderately electronegative, and noble gases are mostly inert with very low electronegativity.

questions.questionText: Consider a bottle containing water, water vapor and air in equilibrium. If the temperature decreases slightly, the amount of water vapor:
options: will decrease and the vapor pressure will increase.
will increase and the vapor pressure will decrease.
questions.explanation:
In a closed container at equilibrium, the vapor pressure of water depends only on temperature.

 When the temperature decreases, the equilibrium vapor pressure decreases.

 As a result, some water vapor condenses into liquid water, so the amount of water vapor also decreases.

questions.questionText: Which statement describes the formation of a covalent bond? In covalent bond electrons are
options: transferred from non-metallic atoms to metallic atoms.
transferred from metallic atoms to non-metallic atoms.
questions.explanation:
A covalent bond is formed when two non-metallic atoms share one or more pairs of electrons to achieve a stable electron configuration.

 This sharing allows both atoms to attain noble gas configuration.

questions.questionText: Which of the following assumptions of the kinetic molecular theory of gases explains the high compressibility of gases?
options: Particles are always in random motion.
There is no force of attraction between gas molecules.
The actual volume of gas molecules is negligible.
questions.explanation:
According to the kinetic molecular theory, gas molecules occupy negligible volume compared to the total volume of the container.

 This means there is a lot of empty space between gas particles, allowing the gas to be easily compressed. 

Therefore, the assumption that explains the high compressibility of gases is that the actual volume of gas molecules is negligible.

questions.questionText: A metal block has a mass of 50.0 grams and a volume of 10.0 milliliters. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density equals mass divided by volume. 50.0 grams divided by 10.0 milliliters equals 5.00 grams per milliliter. The answer must have three significant figures because both given values have three significant figures.

questions.questionText: Which element is in period 4, group 2?
questions.explanation: Calcium is in period 4, group 2.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best describes the difference between a scientific law and a scientific theory?
options: law is an educated guess, a theory is a proven fact.
law is only used in physics, a theory is only used in chemistry.
law describes *what* happens, a theory explains *why* it happens.
law has more experimental evidence than a theory.
questions.explanation: A scientific law describes what happens (e.g., the Law of Gravity), while a scientific theory provides a comprehensive, well-tested explanation for why natural phenomena occur (e.g., the Theory of Evolution).

questions.questionText: Which of the following elements was predicted by Mendeléev and discovered later?
questions.explanation: Mendeléev predicted the existence and properties of gallium before it was discovered.

questions.questionText: Which particle contributes most to the mass of an atom?
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons have nearly all the mass of an atom; electrons contribute very little.

questions.questionText: Which trend helps explain why fluorine is more reactive than chlorine?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has smaller atomic radius, so nucleus attracts electrons more strongly, making it more reactive.

questions.questionText: Which atomic model introduced the concept of electron clouds?
questions.explanation: Schrödinger introduced the quantum mechanical model with electron clouds representing probability distributions.

questions.questionText: Which element is predicted by Mendeléev as eka-silicon?
questions.explanation: Mendeléev predicted germanium as eka-silicon.

questions.questionText: What is the mole volume of a gas?
options: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 25°C and pressure, 1 kPa ) which is equal to 22.4 L/mol .
The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 0°C and pressure, 1 kPa ) which is equal to 22.4 L/mol .
The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 25°C and pressure, 1 atm ) which is equal to 22.4 L/mol .
The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 0°C and pressure, 1 atm ) which is equal to 22.4 L/mol .
questions.explanation:
The molar volume of a gas is the volume occupied by one mole of an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure (STP). 

By IUPAC definition, STP is 0°C (273.15 K) and 1 atm pressure.

 At these conditions, one mole of an ideal gas occupies 22.4 L.

questions.questionText: Which property increases down a group?
questions.explanation: Atomic radius increases down a group due to added electron shells.

questions.questionText: Which particle has a positive charge and nearly the same mass as a neutron?
questions.explanation: Protons are positively charged and have mass similar to neutrons.

questions.questionText: Which statement about the relationship between density and temperature is generally true?
questions.explanation: For most substances, as temperature increases, the volume increases (thermal expansion), while the mass remains constant. Since density equals mass divided by volume, the density decreases.

questions.questionText:
180 g of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) is allowed to react with 156 gram of hydrochloric acid (HCl), according to the following reaction. Which of the following substances is the limiting reagent? (Atomic masses: Ca=40, Cl=35.5, O=16, C=12, H=1)
CaCO3 + 2HCl --> CaCl2 + CO2 + H2O
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following reactions creates energy in our bodies during respiration?
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: What is the approximate mass of a neutron?
questions.explanation: A neutron has a mass close to 1 atomic mass unit (amu).

questions.questionText: Which of the following elements has the highest first ionization energy?
questions.explanation: Neon has the highest first ionization energy due to its stable noble gas configuration.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is responsible for electrolyte conductivity?
options: Ions strongly held in a fixed position.
questions.explanation:
The conductivity of an electrolyte is due to the movement of ions in the solution.

 Positive ions (cations) move toward the cathode, and negative ions (anions) move toward the anode, allowing electric current to flow.

 Electrons held in a fixed position or free electrons in metals do not contribute to electrolyte conductivity.

questions.questionText: Which of the following would occur during the formation of ions?
options: The electronic configuration of an atom forming the ion remains unaffected.
Valence electrons are transferred from one atom to another.
Inner most shell electrons are involved.
Valence electrons are shared between atoms.
questions.explanation:
During the formation of ions, atoms gain or lose electrons to achieve a stable electronic configuration, usually that of a noble gas.

 This involves the transfer of valence electrons from one atom to another. 

Inner electrons are generally not involved, and sharing of electrons occurs in covalent bonding, not ionic formation.

questions.questionText: Which of these has the smallest atomic radius: F, O, N, C?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the smallest atomic radius due to strongest nuclear attraction in the period.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an element with high electron affinity?
questions.explanation: Chlorine has high electron affinity as it readily gains an electron.

questions.questionText: What is enthalpy change? It is
options: the amount of heat absorbed in a reaction.
the amount of heat given out or absorbed in a reaction at constant pressure and volume.
the amount of heat given out or absorbed in a reaction at constant pressure.
the amount of heat given out in a reaction.
questions.explanation:
Enthalpy change (ΔH) is defined as the heat change that occurs during a chemical reaction carried out at constant pressure. 

It represents the difference in enthalpy between products and reactants.

questions.questionText: Convert 750 milliliters to cubic centimeters.
questions.explanation: Since 1 milliliter is exactly equal to 1 cubic centimeter, 750 milliliters is equal to 750 cubic centimeters.

questions.questionText: The first successful prediction of an element’s properties based on periodic table was for:
questions.explanation: Mendeléev predicted properties for both gallium and germanium successfully.

questions.questionText: Who discovered the proton?
questions.explanation: Rutherford discovered the proton as the positively charged particle in the nucleus.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements correctly describes Boyle's Law?
options: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is inversely proportional to the square root of the applied pressure.
The volume of a gas at a given temperature is proportional to the square root of the applied pressure.
The volume of a gas at a given temperature is inversely proportional to the applied pressure.
The volume of a gas at a given temperature is directly proportional to the applied pressure.
questions.explanation:
Boyle's Law states that for a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, the volume of the gas is inversely proportional to its pressure (V ∝ 1/P).

 As pressure increases, volume decreases, and vice versa.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best describes isotopes?
options: Atoms with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
Atoms with the same number of electrons
Atoms with different numbers of protons
Molecules with the same chemical formula
questions.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.

questions.questionText: Electron affinity generally:
questions.explanation: Electron affinity increases across a period and decreases down a group.

questions.questionText: The term 'parallax' refers to an error in measurement caused by:
options: Reading a scale from an angle rather than straight on.
questions.explanation: Parallax error occurs when the observer's eye is not directly perpendicular to the measurement mark, leading to an incorrect reading.

questions.questionText: What is the result of 1.25 + 0.057 + 12.0 when rounded to the correct number of decimal places?
questions.explanation: The sum is 13.307. The least precise number is 12.0, which has one decimal place. Therefore, the result must be rounded to one decimal place, which is 13.3.

questions.questionText: Which law is demonstrated by the reaction: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O?
questions.explanation: The total mass of reactants equals the mass of products, demonstrating the Law of Conservation of Mass.

questions.questionText: Which trend is observed for metallic character across a period?
questions.explanation: Metallic character decreases across a period as elements become less metallic.

questions.questionText: Who proposed the plum pudding model of the atom?
questions.explanation: J.J. Thomson proposed the plum pudding model where electrons are embedded in a positive sphere.

questions.questionText: An isotope of an element differs from the element in:
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following forms of energy change occurs from the combustion of carbon in oxygen is
questions.explanation:
The combustion of carbon in oxygen (C + O₂ → CO₂) is an exothermic chemical reaction that releases energy in the form of heat. 

This heat energy can be used for heating, industrial processes, or generating electricity.

questions.questionText: An element is located in Group VIIA and 3 rd period of the modern periodic table. On the basis of this the element:
options: generally forms an ion with -2 charges.
questions.explanation:
An element in Group VIIA (the halogens) and 3rd period is chlorine (Cl).

 Halogens generally form acidic oxides (e.g., Cl₂O, Cl₂O₃, Cl₂O₇). 

They have high electron affinity, typically form ions with -1 charge, and have high ionization energy, not very low.

questions.questionText: What are intermolecular forces? They are forces due to the attraction between
questions.explanation:
Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction or repulsion that act between neighboring molecules.

 These forces include Van der Waals forces (dispersion forces, dipole-dipole interactions) and hydrogen bonding, all of which occur between molecules.

questions.questionText: How is hydrogen bonding formed? It is formed when a hydrogen atom is bonded to
options: highly electronegative elements, fluorine, oxygen and nitrogen.
highly electronegative elements, chlorine, oxygen and nitrogen.
highly electronegative elements, fluorine oxygen and phosphorus.
highly electronegative elements, fluorine, chlorine and oxygen.
questions.explanation:
Hydrogen bonding occurs when a hydrogen atom is covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom such as fluorine, oxygen, or nitrogen.

 The large difference in electronegativity creates a partial positive charge on hydrogen, which can then interact with lone pairs on nearby electronegative atoms, forming a hydrogen bond.

questions.questionText: Which scientist proposed the 'plum pudding' model of the atom?
questions.explanation: J.J. Thomson proposed that electrons are embedded in a positively charged 'soup' in 1904.

questions.questionText: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity: Li, Be, B, C?
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period; carbon is furthest right, so it has the highest.

questions.questionText: Which of the following trends generally increases across a period?
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period as atoms hold electrons more tightly.

questions.questionText: A student measures the length of an object as 15.5 centimeters, but the actual length is 15.0 centimeters. The magnitude of the absolute error is:
questions.explanation: Absolute error is the absolute difference between the measured value and the true value. Absolute value of (15.5 cm minus 15.0 cm) equals 0.5 cm.

questions.questionText: Which particle was discovered using the oil drop experiment?
questions.explanation: Millikan's oil drop experiment measured the charge of the electron.

questions.questionText: The nucleus of an atom contains:
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons, while electrons orbit around it.

questions.questionText: A beaker is generally used for which purpose in a laboratory?
questions.explanation: Beakers are general-purpose glassware, used primarily for holding, mixing, and heating solutions. They are not accurate for precise volume measurements.

questions.questionText: Which of these is a fundamental law of chemical reactions?
questions.explanation: The Law of Definite Proportions is a fundamental law in chemistry describing fixed mass ratios in compounds.

questions.questionText: Which element is most reactive in Group 1?
questions.explanation: Reactivity increases down the group; cesium is most reactive.

questions.questionText: Which experiment proved the existence of the atomic nucleus?
questions.explanation: Rutherford's gold foil experiment showed that atoms have a dense central nucleus.

questions.questionText: A type of reaction in which two compounds react together to form two or more products by exchanging reactants' ions is known as
questions.explanation:
A double displacement reaction occurs when two compounds exchange ions to form two new compounds.

 For example, AB + CD → AD + CB. 

- Decomposition reaction: a single compound breaks down into simpler substances.

- Combination reaction: two or more reactants combine to form one product.

- Single displacement reaction: an element replaces another in a compound.

questions.questionText: Who suggested that atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios?
questions.explanation: Dalton's atomic theory stated that atoms combine in simple ratios to form compounds.

questions.questionText: What is the basis of the modern periodic law?
questions.explanation: Modern periodic law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.

questions.questionText: Which of these is a property of non-metals?
questions.explanation: Non-metals are poor conductors of heat and electricity.

questions.questionText: The standard deviation of a set of measurements is a measure of:
questions.explanation: Standard deviation quantifies the amount of variation or dispersion of a set of data values. A smaller standard deviation indicates higher precision.

questions.questionText: A chemical bond that results from the attractive force between shared electrons and nonmetal nuclei is called a
questions.explanation:
A covalent bond forms when two nonmetal atoms share valence electrons, and the shared electrons are **attracted to the nuclei of both atoms, holding them together. 

Ionic bonds result from electron transfer, hydrogen bonds are intermolecular attractions, and metallic bonds involve a 'sea of electrons' in metals.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a base unit in the SI system?
questions.explanation: The liter is a metric unit of volume, but the SI base unit of volume is the cubic meter (a derived unit), making the liter a non-base unit.

questions.questionText: Which law explains why water is always H₂O, regardless of source?
questions.explanation: The Law of Definite Proportions states that a chemical compound always contains elements in a fixed ratio.

questions.questionText: Which group contains the halogens?
questions.explanation: Halogens are in Group 17.

questions.questionText: Which period contains the lanthanides?
questions.explanation: Lanthanides are in period 6.

questions.questionText: A reaction that involves the exchange of positive and negative ions of each reactant is a definition of a
questions.explanation: A double displacement reaction involves the exchange of positive and negative ions between two compounds to form new compounds. For example, AB + CD → AD + CB. Single displacement involves one element replacing another, decomposition breaks a compound into simpler substances, and combination reactions form a single product from two or more reactants.

questions.questionText: The concept that the physical properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic number is known as the:
questions.explanation: The Modern Periodic Law, based on the work of Henry Moseley, states that elemental properties repeat periodically when arranged by increasing atomic number.

questions.questionText: Which experiment led to the discovery of the electron?
questions.explanation: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron through the cathode ray tube experiment.

questions.questionText: Which law states that atoms of one element can combine with atoms of another element in simple ratios to form different compounds?
questions.explanation: The Law of Multiple Proportions describes mass ratios in different compounds of the same elements.

questions.questionText: Which scientist discovered the nucleus using alpha particles?
questions.explanation: Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment revealed the dense nucleus.

questions.questionText: Which model explained the discrete spectral lines of hydrogen?
questions.explanation: Bohr's model introduced quantized energy levels to explain hydrogen spectral lines.

questions.questionText: What is oxidation? Oxidation is
options: the reduction of the oxidation state of the oxidizing agent.
the addition of electron(s) to the oxidizing agent.
the loss of electrons by a species, accompanied by an increase in oxidation number.
the addition of hydrogen to a substance and the removal of oxygen from a substance.
questions.explanation:
Oxidation is defined as the process in which a species loses electrons, resulting in an increase in its oxidation number.

 This is a key concept in redox reactions.

questions.questionText: How many millimeters are there in 5.2 centimeters?
questions.explanation: Since 1 centimeter equals 10 millimeters, multiply 5.2 by 10 to get 52 millimeters.

questions.questionText: Which group in the periodic table contains noble gases?
questions.explanation: Group 18 contains noble gases, which are chemically inert.

questions.questionText: Which element is the most reactive non-metal?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most reactive non-metal due to its high electronegativity.

questions.questionText: The smallest particle of an element that retains the chemical properties of that element is the:
questions.explanation: An atom is the smallest unit of matter that characteristically retains the chemical properties of an element.

questions.questionText: What is the standard laboratory instrument used to determine the mass of a substance accurately?
options: Triple beam balance or electronic balance
questions.explanation: Balances (electronic or triple beam) are calibrated instruments specifically designed to measure mass.

questions.questionText: Which period has 18 elements?
questions.explanation: Period 4 contains 18 elements (transition elements included).

questions.questionText: Compare reactivity of Cl and F. More reactive is:
questions.explanation: Fluorine is more reactive due to higher electronegativity and smaller size.

questions.questionText: Which isotope of hydrogen has no neutrons?
questions.explanation: Protium (¹H) has one proton and no neutrons.

questions.questionText: If electronegativity of F = 3.98 and Cl = 3.16, trend is:
questions.explanation: Electronegativity decreases down the group; F > Cl.

questions.questionText: Who proposed the first atomic theory of matter?
questions.explanation: John Dalton proposed the first atomic theory around 1803, suggesting that matter is made of indivisible atoms.

questions.questionText: In the formation of the compound Lithium fluoride (L i F), the Lithium atom:
questions.explanation: Lithium (Group 1, a metal) loses its one valence electron to form a L i one plus cation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is true about metals and non-metals?
options: Metals are brittle, non-metals are malleable
Metals are good conductors, non-metals are poor conductors
Non-metals have low electronegativity, metals have high
Metals are non-lustrous, non-metals are shiny
questions.explanation: Metals are good conductors; non-metals are generally poor conductors of electricity and heat.

questions.questionText: Which of the following represents the most basic level of matter studied in chemistry?
questions.explanation: An element is a pure substance consisting only of atoms that all have the same numbers of protons (atomic number), representing the fundamental building blocks.

questions.questionText: In the scientific method, what is the step that involves proposing a tentative, testable explanation for an observation?
questions.explanation: A hypothesis is an educated guess or a proposed, tentative explanation that can be tested through controlled experimentation.

questions.questionText: Convert 2.5 kilometers to centimeters.
questions.explanation:
Start with 2.5 kilometers.
 Multiply by 1000 to convert to meters (2500 meters).
 Multiply by 100 to convert to centimeters (250,000 centimeters).
 The conversion factor is 1 kilometer = 100,000 centimeters.

questions.questionText: If ionization energy of Al = 578 kJ/mol and Si = 786 kJ/mol, which is correct?
questions.explanation: Ionization energy increases across a period; Si > Al.
